description: A Python3 script that uses fitburst API to read, preprocess, and fit 'generic'-formatted data against a model of the dynamic spectrum. NOTE: by default, the scattering timescale is not a fit parameter but can be turned into one through use of the --fit option.

arguments.name: file
arguments.help: A Numpy state file containing data and metadata in fitburst-compliant ('generic') format.

arguments.name: --amplitude
arguments.help: Initial guess for log (base 10) of the overall amplitude.

arguments.name: --arrival_time
arguments.help: Initial guess for arrival time, in units of seconds.

arguments.name: --dm
arguments.help: Initial guess for DM, in units of pc/cc.

arguments.name: --dm_index
arguments.help: Initial guess for index DM time delay, in units of dex.

arguments.name: --downsample_freq
arguments.help: Downsample the raw spectrum along the frequency axis by a specified integer.

arguments.name: --downsample_time
arguments.help: Downsample the raw spectrum along the time axis by a specified integer.

arguments.name: --fit
arguments.help: A list of assumed-fixed model parameters to fit during least-squares estimation.

arguments.name: --fix
arguments.help: A list of model parameters to hold fixed to initial values.

arguments.name: --folded
arguments.help: If set, then fit spectrum of a folded profile (e.g., for a pulsar observation).

arguments.name: --iterations
arguments.help: Integer number of fit iterations.

arguments.name: --outfile
arguments.help: If set, then use substring to uniquely label output filenamese based on input filenames.

arguments.name: --peakfind_dist
arguments.help: Separation used for peak-finding algorithm (for multi-component fitting).

arguments.name: --peakfind_rms
arguments.help: RMS used for peak-finding algorithm (for multi-component fitting).

arguments.name: --preprocess
arguments.help: If set, the run preprocessing return to normalize data and mask bad frequencies.

arguments.name: --ref_freq
arguments.help: If set, then replace reference frequency with command-line value.

arguments.name: --remove_smearing
arguments.help: If set, then allow for removal of dispersion smearing.

arguments.name: --scattering_timescale
arguments.help: Initial guess for scattering timescale, in units of seconds.

arguments.name: --scintillation
arguments.help: If set, then allow amplitude-independent modelling to account for scintillation.

arguments.name: --spectral_index
arguments.help: Initial guess for power-law spectral index.

arguments.name: --spectral_running
arguments.help: Initial guess for power-law spectral 'running'.

arguments.name: --solution
arguments.help: If set, use existing solution in fitburst-compliant JSON format.

arguments.name: --upsample_freq
arguments.help: Upsample the raw spectrum along the frequency axis by a specified integer.

arguments.name: --upsample_time
arguments.help: Upsample the raw spectrum along the time axis by a specified integer.

arguments.name: --variance_range
arguments.help: Bounds of per-channel variance used to designate 'bad' channels in preprocessing step.

arguments.name: --verbose
arguments.help: If set, then print additional information related to fit parameters and fitting.

arguments.name: --weight_range
arguments.help: Indeces for timestamp array that represent region to evaluate RMS data weights.

arguments.name: --width
arguments.help: Initial guess for burst width, in seconds.

arguments.name: --window
arguments.help: Half of size of data window, in seconds.
